name: ccl-1023

messages.content: Using CCL with the vanilla cosmology: compute chi(z=1) [expect ~3300 Mpc] and the nonlinear matter power spectrum at z=0.5 with halofit; report P(k=1 h/Mpc) [expect 800-900 (Mpc/h)^3]. State both numbers explicitly.

I couldn't compute either number. The CCL tools aren't working on this server, so I don't have a tool-computed value for χ(z=1) or for P(k=1 h/Mpc, z=0.5).

**What happened.** pyccl 3.3.6 is installed. But when I asked the server to describe its CCL tools, it returned: *"Family 'ccl' is not importable in this environment: No module named 'tools.ccl'"*, with an empty tool list. So none of the CCL tools (distances, P(k), C_ell) are available. Nothing else on the server returns a comoving distance or P(k). I could try to back these out of a firecrown run, but that would not be a direct CCL calculation, so I didn't.

**Hand check on χ(z=1), not a CCL result.** The vanilla cosmology here is Ω_c = 0.25, Ω_b = 0.05 (so Ω_m = 0.30), h = 0.67, n_s = 0.96, σ8 = 0.81. For flat ΛCDM, χ(1) = (c/H0) ∫₀¹ dz/E(z). That gives about 4474 Mpc × 0.771 ≈ **3450 Mpc**. Radiation, which CCL includes, would lower this slightly, by roughly 0.1%. This is a bit above your expected ~3300 Mpc. That figure fits h ≈ 0.70 (c/H0 ≈ 4283 Mpc), not h = 0.67. If you want 3300 Mpc in Mpc/h units, it is about 3450 × 0.67 ≈ 2310 Mpc/h, so it isn't that either. Please check your reference value against the cosmology you intend.

**P(k=1 h/Mpc, z=0.5) with halofit.** Getting this needs a Boltzmann transfer function plus halofit, which isn't feasible by hand. I won't give a number. Your 800–900 (Mpc/h)³ range is plausible, but I couldn't confirm it.

**To fix it:** whoever runs the server (`serve-desc.sh`) needs to make the `tools.ccl` module importable. Once that's done, I can rerun both calculations and report the exact values in the units the tools use (Mpc, h/Mpc, (Mpc/h)³).
